scope: Read-only review of the frozen six-file CI prototype, actual GitHub Actions receipts, GitHub's official GITHUB_TOKEN and workflow-dispatch documentation, and local artifact acceptance predicates. No workflow dispatch, source edits, builds, or tests were performed.
verdict_A_reason: The repair path can report already-covered and skip dispatch while its only exact-source CI run is still in progress. It also treats any matching workflow_dispatch actor as coverage, while artifact import accepts workflow_dispatch only from github-actions[bot]. Either case can leave a released source without an importable successful artifact.

confirmed.finding: The underlying GitHub-token push gap is real.
confirmed.evidence: GitHub Actions runs API filtered by exact SHA e39cedba10360c57135dd937b19a3ad5509504e3 returned total_count=0. For 6adb65d53f1b8047545c1361fb0fdfd9455a1016 the API returned exactly one run, 39659073385, whose path is .github/workflows/release.yml; there is no CI run for that SHA. A nearby human push SHA 5eb78e8aa559450cd92475989f349c3705843059 has CI run 39659840121. Official GitHub docs state GITHUB_TOKEN-triggered push events do not start new workflows, with workflow_dispatch and repository_dispatch as exceptions.

confirmed.finding: The dedup predicate does not guarantee artifact-acceptable coverage.
confirmed.evidence: scripts/release-development-ci.mjs accepts a matching run when status is not completed, and the new test explicitly expects an in_progress run to return already-covered. scripts/current-test-artifact.mjs:verifyGitHubMetadata requires status=completed and conclusion=success. The dispatch predicate also accepts any actor for workflow_dispatch, but artifact verification rejects workflow_dispatch unless actor.login is github-actions[bot]. Align coverage with the importer acceptance predicate; an in-progress run must not be considered completed coverage, and non-bot dispatches cannot cover this release path.

confirmed.finding: Workflow-dispatch API permission and recursion mechanism are directionally correct.
confirmed.evidence: The release workflow adds actions:write and invokes the existing ci.yml workflow_dispatch endpoint with ref main and the exact source SHA. GitHub's REST workflow-dispatch documentation requires Actions write permission; official GITHUB_TOKEN documentation exempts workflow_dispatch from recursion suppression.

confirmed.finding: The prototype preserves the main exact-source checks and existing full CI lanes in source.
confirmed.evidence: Pinned diff dispatches only when current main equals receipt.sourceSha; the dispatched scope job asserts refs/heads/main and expected SHA equality before dependent work; full checks and resource-guard-integration run for non-doc scopes; artifact producer and importer bind run.head_sha to the exact source. Scope also changes downstream job conditions from always() to scope success, avoiding checks after failed source validation.

confirmed.finding: Declared cost increment fits the stated ceiling for this change.
confirmed.evidence: Pinned cost manifest estimates at most 13 additional full CI runs per week, about $1.51/week at list prices, and $0 billed increment because this repository is public. The dispatch reuses ci.yml and creates no polling loop or additional schedule. The hosted artifact and actual run remain unobserved.
